title: Boiler 1 Feed-Water Quality Maintenance

sections.heading: Check first
items: Test the feed-water conductivity and hardness immediately.
Compare the conductivity reading against the machine's normal levels from the last 30 days.
Check if the softener or resin bed is due for regeneration.
Verify the current blowdown schedule and check that blowdown valves are operating.

sections.heading: Step by step
items: Use the test reagent kit to measure current water quality.
Regenerate the softener or resin bed if it is past its service interval.
Increase the blowdown rate to lower the concentration of dissolved solids.
Dissolved solids are minerals in the water that can form scale.
Adjust the chemical dosing rates to match the mill's water-treatment plan.
Record all test results and actions taken in the work order.

sections.heading: Safety
items: If any machine parts must be opened, perform lock-out/tag-out first.
Isolate all energy sources including electrical, steam, and hydraulic pressure.
Lock, tag, and test that the equipment cannot move.
Follow the mill's SOP for handling water-treatment chemicals.

sections.heading: Parts and tools
items: Resin or softener salt.
Test reagent kit.
Manufacturer's manual for water quality limits.
Mill's SOP for dosing and blowdown procedures.

sections.heading: Call the manufacturer if
items: Conductivity stays high after increasing the blowdown frequency.
Water hardness levels do not return to the limits defined in the mill's SOP.
You suspect scale has already built up on the boiler tubes.
Scale is a mineral layer that insulates tubes and can cause them to overheat and fail.
